tasks.short: Prepare and edit employee newsletters and external organizational reports.

steps.what: Request and collect contributor submissions through the {EMAIL}.
Reconcile emailed contributor versions into a source pack in the {DOCS}.
Agree audience, emphasis and sensitive omissions with the public relations manager.
Write the publication draft in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Approved editorial outline, permission-filtered source pack and style guide.
loop.output: Publication draft with source references and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Check source references, numbers and quotations; a person reviews meaning and omissions.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per section; unsupported content returns to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates assemble sections, but varied contributor prose needs synthesis and audience-specific wording.

steps.what: Correct spelling, terminology and house style in the {DOCS}.
Verify claims, quotations and permissions against the source pack in the {DOCS}.
Approve the exact publication version through the {EMAIL}.
Publish approved material through the {CMS} or distribute through the {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: Configure contributor intake in the {WORKFLOW} and keep canonical submissions in the {DOCS}, removing emailed version reconciliation. A template generator uses a bounded drafting loop, followed by configured style checks and human verification. The {WORKFLOW} releases through the {CMS} or {EMAIL} only when the exact version and destination have approval; later edits invalidate that approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Templates could format publications, but fragmented submissions and varied prose still required manual assembly and rewriting.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing intake and publishing controls can handle coordination. AI-assisted coding reduces assembly work, while a bounded model can draft from a controlled source pack.
tasks.still_hard: Sensitive omissions, financial disclosures, quotation permissions and audience trust require judgement. GDPR applies to employee material; public-interest AI text may require transparency under the EU AI Act.
tasks.human_edge: Choose what matters to readers, challenge misleading framing and protect contributors whose stories carry personal risk.

ambition.what: A plain-language newsletter edition for frontline employees with limited reading time.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from collecting versions and correcting copy to interviewing contributors and assessing audience needs. Release and financial-disclosure decision rights remain with the existing approvers.

reach.task: Build an issue outline around reader questions.
reach.learn: Commissioning, narrative order and evidence-preserving cuts.
Heading structure, reading order and accessible export checks.

evidence.claim: Configured spelling and grammar checks can handle routine corrections.
Acrolinx supports repeatable house-style scoring and quality gates.
The MIT writing trial included press releases, reports and emails; its gains do not establish whole-task savings here.
Canonical contributor records and version-bound publishing approvals are feasible workflow patterns.

assumptions: Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured customer results.
Document work dominates, as the priors suggest; source verification and release judgement remain substantial.
Routine publications have reusable sections and an approved style guide.
Existing model access permits the relevant internal data under GDPR-compliant controls.
Access work includes contributor permissions and employee consultation where national rules require it.
Employee content does not receive a general journalistic exemption from GDPR.
unknowns: Publication types, languages, volumes and approval roles.
Whether shareholder reports require additional finance or legal approvals.
Available intake, document and publishing permissions.
Current style rules, quotation permissions and distribution-list ownership.
Applicable national consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which source-reference checks reliably catch altered numbers and invented quotations?
Which sections can use fixed templates without weakening reader comprehension?
new_work: Review model drafts and unresolved source questions.
Maintain templates, terminology and contributor intake fields.
Check distribution failures and stale approvals.
Maintain permissions, retention rules and connector access.

tasks.short: Arrange public appearances and events that build awareness and goodwill.

steps.what: Agree event objectives, audience and constraints with the client or public relations manager.
Compare venues and appearance opportunities in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Discuss availability, audience fit and terms with hosts and speakers.
Approve the event budget and proposed terms in the {DOCS}.
Confirm approved bookings and record supplier acknowledgements through the {EMAIL}.
Maintain the event schedule, responsibilities and logistics checklist in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Prepare speaker briefs and the running order in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Confirmed schedule, event objectives and approved organizational facts.
loop.output: Speaker brief with sourced talking points; running order assembled from confirmed timings.
loop.check: Validate timings and names against booking records; specialist checks tone and factual support.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing facts remain explicit questions.
loop.why_not_simpler: The running order is deterministic, but audience-specific talking points need prose adaptation.

steps.what: Coordinate setup, brief hosts and resolve live changes at the venue.

tasks.design: Create event records in the {WORKFLOW}, with rule-based opportunity filters, approved booking fields and a reusable logistics checklist linked to the {PROJECT} and {CALENDAR}. Deterministic templates prepare confirmations, while a bounded loop drafts speaker briefs in the {DOCS}. Exact spending commitments require budget-owner approval; relationship discussions and live coordination stay with people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Event software could track dates, but supplier terms, approvals and responsibilities were scattered across conversations and separate files.
tasks.enabler_now: A small records app and existing workflow features can connect those artefacts. A bounded drafting loop handles the variable wording of speaker briefs.
tasks.still_hard: Audience fit, negotiation and live changes remain situational. Unstructured supplier acknowledgements and nonstandard contracts still need manual handling.
tasks.human_edge: Earn cooperation from hosts and speakers, negotiate trade-offs and respond calmly when plans change.

ambition.what: A repeatable community speaker programme for local associations.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time maintaining schedules and more time developing hosts and preparing speakers. Spending and contractual decision rights remain with the budget owner.

reach.task: Build a venue readiness plan and contingency schedule.
reach.learn: Supplier dependencies, accessibility requirements and escalation timing.

reach.task: Evaluate which appearances support a communication objective.
reach.learn: Audience fit, reputational trade-offs and outcome-based evaluation.

evidence.claim: Event records, checklist templates, calendar synchronization and approval-bound confirmations are deterministic workflow patterns.
The MIT writing trial supports bounded assistance with professional prose, but provides no evidence for automating event negotiation.

assumptions: Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
The people-heavy prior is retained; paperwork can change independently of the conversations.
Shortlist filters use explicit constraints and maintained records; a person assesses audience fit.
Only confirmations matching approved supplier, amount, date and terms can be sent automatically.
Ambiguous acknowledgements and changed terms return to a person.
GDPR applies to contact and attendee data; national rules determine consultation requirements.
The specialist has existing delegated authority for nonbinding discussions and live coordination.
unknowns: Existing event records, approved suppliers and booking channels.
Spending limits and contract-signing authority.
Access to shared calendars and event contact records.
Typical frequency of cancellations and nonstandard terms.
Applicable attendee-data and employee-consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which booking confirmations can use structured fields without losing contractual meaning?
Which readiness checks predict preventable event failures?
new_work: Maintain opportunity records, supplier details and checklist templates.
Review changed terms and unclear supplier acknowledgements.
Resolve calendar synchronization and notification failures.
Review speaker drafts before sharing them.

tasks.short: Research public opinion and market response, then explain findings to management or clients.

steps.what: Agree the research question and intended management decision.
Design the questionnaire, sample approach and interview guide in the {DOCS}.
Select eligible customer contacts from the {CRM} using the research protocol.
Launch the approved questionnaire and invitations in survey software, an {OTHER} system.
Monitor responses and send reminders in survey software, an {OTHER} system.
Conduct interviews and record participant explanations.
Clean survey exports and check exclusions in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Code open responses and interview themes in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: De-identified responses, interview notes and a fixed coding guide.
loop.output: Proposed codes, supporting excerpts and unresolved responses.
loop.check: Verify excerpt locations; review a stratified sample, rare themes and ambiguous cases.
loop.stop: One classification and one repair pass per batch; unresolved or novel themes go to the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Respondents express the same idea in varied language; keyword rules miss context and negation.

steps.what: Calculate results and compare respondent groups in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Write findings and recommendations in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Validated tables, approved theme evidence and explicit analysis limitations.
loop.output: Draft findings with traceable table references and tentative recommendations.
loop.check: Match every number to a table; analyst checks uncertainty, representativeness and causal language.
loop.stop: One report draft and one repair pass; unsupported conclusions are removed or returned to the analyst.
loop.why_not_simpler: Tables can be templated, but explaining mixed findings needs contextual prose.

steps.what: Explain findings, limitations and proposed actions to management or the client.

tasks.design: Configure contact eligibility in the {CRM} and survey collection in the {OTHER}; a scheduled job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} cleans exports, records exclusions and calculates tables for the {BI}. Small bounded loops propose qualitative codes and draft a report in the {DOCS} from validated evidence. A research lead approves study launch, while interviews, methodological judgement and management discussion remain human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Collection tools existed, but repeatable export cleaning and qualitative coding were disconnected from report preparation. Study quality also depended on expertise that software could not supply.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic pipelines can reuse approved cleaning and analysis rules. Bounded language processing can propose codes and explain validated results without controlling the research design.
tasks.still_hard: Sampling bias, leading questions and nonresponse can invalidate efficient analysis. GDPR applies to respondent data, and employee research may require consultation under national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Ask a useful question, notice what respondents hesitate to say and distinguish an interesting pattern from a defensible conclusion.

ambition.what: Quarterly message-comprehension decisions before campaign spending.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time cleaning exports and assembling reports, and more time testing explanations with respondents. Management retains product and spending decisions; methodological authority requires agreed delegation.

reach.task: Design a sample and assess uncertainty in subgroup results.
reach.learn: Sampling error, nonresponse bias, weighting limits and qualitative coding validation.

reach.task: Translate research findings into a campaign decision.
reach.learn: Decision thresholds, commercial trade-offs and the cost of acting on weak evidence.

evidence.claim: Eligibility filters, response reminders, export cleaning and statistical tables can use configured or deterministic tools.
Bounded models can propose qualitative codes, but local validation is needed before relying on those codes.
The MIT trial supports assistance with report writing; it does not validate sampling or research conclusions.

assumptions: Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
This baseline is a modest mixed-method study using a customer sample; broader public sampling may need an external research provider.
The specialist leads routine studies and obtains research-method support when needed.
The lower rule-coverage prior applies to design and interpretation, while cleaning and calculations are more structured.
Survey software is represented by the {OTHER} slot.
Reminder timing, suppression and maximum frequency are approved before launch.
Model inputs are de-identified where possible, with GDPR-compliant access and retention controls.
EU AI Act obligations are assessed for the actual use; the design does not infer employee traits or make employment decisions.
unknowns: Research scope, respondent populations and current methodological support.
Lawful basis, contact permissions and retention periods.
Available survey exports, contact fields and integration access.
Approved exclusion, weighting and subgroup-reporting rules.
National rules for employee surveys and consultation.
Who may approve studies and issue external research reports.
research_questions: How accurately does proposed coding preserve minority views and contradictory responses?
Which validation sample detects material coding errors at acceptable review cost?
What study design can support quarterly comparisons without confusing sample changes with opinion changes?
new_work: Validate proposed codes and adjudicate ambiguous responses.
Maintain questionnaires, cleaning rules and analysis specifications.
Check suppression, reminders and respondent-data retention.
Monitor sample composition and document limitations.
Revalidate coding after changes to the model or coding guide.

tasks.short: Plan and write communications about environmental, safety and social activities.

steps.what: Collect activity evidence and stakeholder concerns through the {EMAIL}.
Check claim scope, measurement boundaries and supporting evidence in the {DOCS}.
Agree audiences, emphasis and responses to likely criticism.
Draft channel materials and stakeholder answers in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Communication plan, verified claims with scope and dates, and approved style guide.
loop.output: Channel drafts and stakeholder answers linked to claim records.
loop.check: Match figures and claim identifiers; specialist checks qualifications, tone and omitted limitations.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per channel; unsupported claims remain questions.
loop.why_not_simpler: Claim fields are structured, but explaining them to different audiences needs contextual wording.

steps.what: Check grammar, approved terminology and house style in the {DOCS}.
Approve final wording and release channels through the {EMAIL}.
Publish approved materials through the {CMS} and schedule posts in the {SOCIAL}.

tasks.design: Use the {WORKFLOW} to collect evidence into a claim register in the {DOCS}, including scope, owner, dates and limitations. A bounded generator drafts channel materials from verified claims, and configured style checks prepare review. Approval binds the exact text and channels before the {CMS} and {SOCIAL} publish; changed or expired claims block reuse.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence was scattered and claim qualifications lived in conversations. Templates could format statements but could not decide whether their implications were defensible.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured claim records and deterministic freshness checks make evidence reusable. A bounded drafting loop can adapt approved facts while preserving their qualifications.
tasks.still_hard: Environmental and social claims can mislead through scope or omissions even when individual facts are correct. Safety implications, GDPR and applicable EU and national claim rules still require expert judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize the gap between an activity and a meaningful benefit, hear stakeholder objections and insist on honest limitations.

ambition.what: A public progress page linking environmental commitments to dated supporting evidence.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends more time testing claims with subject matter specialists and stakeholders, and less time assembling channel copy. Claim acceptance and external release rights remain with the designated specialists and manager.

reach.task: Define the scope and evidence behind an environmental claim.
reach.learn: Measurement boundaries, baselines, comparison periods and material limitations.

reach.task: Explain safety activities without obscuring conditions or exceptions.
reach.learn: Precise qualifications, reader comprehension checks and evidence traceability.

evidence.claim: Acrolinx supports repeatable style checks and quality gates.
Coosto supports post scheduling; this does not establish claim-verification capability.
Full Fact AI identifies checkable claims and matches repeats; it does not certify an organization's environmental claims.
Claim registers, expiry checks and version-bound release approvals are feasible deterministic controls.

assumptions: Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
The high automation prior applies mainly to assembly and drafting; claim acceptance and stakeholder judgement remain human.
A subject matter specialist can verify evidence before drafting begins.
The claim register records boundaries and limitations, not just supporting links.
GDPR controls apply to stakeholder feedback and personal stories.
EU AI Act transparency obligations are assessed before publication, including any editorial-responsibility exception.
Access work includes evidence permissions and employee consultation where national rules require it.
unknowns: Current evidence owners, measurement definitions and claim-approval roles.
Which claims require legal or safety review.
Whether source records have dates, limitations and reuse permissions.
Available publishing access and approval controls.
Applicable sector rules, national rules and consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which checks detect lost qualifications when approved claims are shortened for a channel?
How can stale evidence be detected without treating every unchanged claim as invalid?
Which evidence presentation helps readers understand both progress and limitations?
new_work: Maintain claim scope, evidence dates and expiry rules.
Review draft qualifications and unsupported implications.
Handle evidence-owner disputes and missing measurements.
Update or withdraw published claims when evidence changes.

role.altitude: The role shifts toward evidence-led communication, stakeholder conversations and research interpretation. Less time goes to version chasing, scheduling and repetitive drafting; release, spending and methodological rights change only through explicit delegation.
reach: Venue readiness and contingencies with an event planner.
Research design and uncertainty assessment with a market research analyst.
Environmental claim substantiation with a sustainability specialist.
skills_to_grow: Sampling, uncertainty and qualitative coding validation.
GDPR-aware data handling and publication transparency.
role.ambitious_version: Run a small communication evidence service that combines message testing, substantiated public updates and a community speaker programme, with specialist approval at consequential actions.
